messages:
jen: Kickoff for CatalystNova POC — they want to validate microburst behavior + SLA before contract. Need a short load plan, cost sketch, and security checklist. Can ops + sec sync? :wave:

maria: Quick plan draft below. Three phases: 1) soak (sustained 5k qps for 1h) 2) microburst spike (20k qps for 10s, repeated 6x) 3) long tail (12h low-rate run). Measure p50/p95/p99, tail token latency, and error budget. Runbook coming.

kevin: +1 on phases. Important notes: warm KV cache before spike, ensure continuous batching enabled, and run at least one warmup iteration with full context lengths. For dedicated runs, pin model shards to avoid cross-host eviction.

maria: Minimal smoke run commands (you can adapt to k6/wrk):
```
# generate mixed short+long prompts
python tools/loadgen.py --mix "short:70,long:30" --qps 5000 --duration 60m --out results/smoke.json
# spike: 20k qps for 10s x6 bursts
python tools/loadgen.py --burst 20000 --burst-duration 10s --bursts 6 --out results/spike.json
```

kevin: Also set warmup flag: `--warmup 20m` so KV/prefix caches stabilize. Metric collection: GPU util, enqueue wait, avg batch size, and per-request model_variant tag. If you see queue length > 50ms consistently, backoff or route to fallback model.

oliver: Pricing/practical: microburst minutes matter. Finance needs an estimate of peak-minute usage to price burst capacity. Jen, confirm if CatalystNova is comfortable with ~2k burst-minutes/month or if they need a hard cap.

jen: They're willing to start with a 2k burst-minutes budget for the POC window but want a per-10k-token cost estimate for that pattern (mix above). Can we generate a quick unit-cost calc from last week's benchmark numbers?

maria: Rough calc from similar runs: with our q4-optimized kernels and batching, microburst unit cost ~ $0.024 per 10k tokens (hosted) vs $0.013 on Dedicated with reserved capacity. I'll run numbers against the exact prompt mix and post updated estimate.

sam: Quick question from CatalystNova: can you replicate our thin-client mix? Most prompts are ~40 tokens, ~70% short replies. Also we use occasional tool calls that add extra round trips.

maria: Yes — include tool-call latency in the end-to-end measurement. Use `--prompt-len 40 --reply-len 60` and add a 2-3x small-request burst to simulate user spikes. Example mix JSON: 
```
{"mix": [{"type":"short","weight":70,"prompt_tokens":40,"response_tokens":60},{"type":"long","weight":30,"prompt_tokens":200,"response_tokens":250}], "tool_calls_pct": 8}
```

sec-bot: Security questionnaire v2 uploaded: https://redwood-inference.internal/sq/789 — check items 3.2 (KMS/HSM) and 4.1 (audit logs retention). Also note: customer requires SOC2 + IP allowlist for the POC.

jen: I'll loop in our security AE to answer HSM questions. Sam, can you confirm whether CatalystNova needs HSM-backed key storage or customer-managed keys for the POC?

sam: We prefer customer-managed keys (BYOK) if available. HSM recommended but not mandatory for POC. Also need audit log access for each test run.

kevin: For BYOK/HSM: Private deployment supports HSM and KMS integration. Note: HSM KMS calls add ~8-12ms if done per-request unless we cache derived keys. Recommend key-caching layer at the host for POC to avoid per-request roundtrip. I'll document tradeoffs in the security answers.

maria: Ops recommendation: run POC in Dedicated pool with cache warmed and KMS key-caching enabled. That gives predictable latency and lower unit cost. We'll still run one hosted-run to validate fallback routing.

jen: Next steps: Maria + Kevin to post final runbook + test matrix by Wed EOD. Jen to send cost sketch and contract addendum. Sam — aim for smoke run Thurs 10am PST. If any blocker, flag here.

sam: :thumbsup: thanks, looking forward to the runbook and cost numbers.

oliver: I'll pre-allocate a Dedicated slot for Thurs so we can reduce flakiness. Will share the reservation id once done.

maria: Will include dashboard links (latency heatmap, batch size distribution, error traces) in the runbook. Use tag `catalystnova-poc` so we can filter results easily.

jen: Great — closing for now. I'll post follow-ups as they arrive. :lock:
